claims.text: WTaTiVZr is an equimolar refractory high-entropy alloy.
The constituent elements of WTaTiVZr are reduced-activation materials suitable for easier post-service recycling in nuclear applications.
WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature plastic strain and toughness than commercially used pure tungsten.
The improved plastic strain and toughness arise mainly from severe lattice distortion caused by the multi-principal-element composition.
Severe lattice distortion broadens the spectrum of active slip systems in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion facilitates dislocation cross-slip and dynamic recovery at high temperature.
Large atomic-size mismatch in equimolar WTaTiVZr produces substantial lattice strain.
Dislocation-mediated, thermally activated deformation operates in TaTiVWZr under indentation creep loading.
Lattice strain increases the ease of dislocation nucleation and motion in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
Enhanced dislocation mobility distributes plastic deformation and delays localized dislocation pileup, strain localization, and crack initiation.
The proposed WTaTiVZr material is produced by mechanical alloying and spark-plasma sintering.
The processed WTaTiVZr material has a uniform BCC structure with minimal segregation.
The pure-tungsten comparator has a commercially standard microstructure.
Fusion plasma-facing components experience severe high-temperature and mechanical loading that requires exceptional material performance.
The applicable comparison is at temperatures above tungsten's ductile-to-brittle transition temperature.
Nanoindentation creep under static or dynamic load is an applicable high-temperature test for the proposed comparison.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will show larger creep displacement or ductility and higher fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
Replacing pure tungsten with WTaTiVZr while holding processing, geometry, and testing conditions fixed isolates lattice distortion and multi-element solid-solution effects.

contradictions.description: The tungsten comparator is described as commercially produced with a standard microstructure, while other fields require tungsten and the powder-metallurgy HEA to receive identical processing. A commercial tungsten microstructure and identical mechanical-alloying/spark-plasma-sintering histories are not simultaneously specified.

The intervention is claimed to isolate lattice distortion, but replacing pure W with a five-element alloy simultaneously changes chemistry, elemental interactions, defect energetics, and potentially microstructure. No independent manipulation or direct measurement of lattice distortion is specified to distinguish it from these co-varying causes.
